fixedAssumptions.split: FNV-1a(galaxy name) modulo 5; zero is holdout

subqgMicroscopicFlux.equation: C_SubQG(g)*g = gbar; C_SubQG from variational microchannel occupation
subqgMicroscopicFlux.methodologicalNote: a0 = phaseFraction*c*H0 is an existing cosmological bridge ansatz

subqgMinusNewton.unit: mean per-galaxy squared log10 residual difference (modelA - modelB)

subqgMinusEmpiricalRar.unit: mean per-galaxy squared log10 residual difference (modelA - modelB)

microscopicFluxMinusNewton.unit: mean per-galaxy squared log10 residual difference (modelA - modelB)

microscopicFluxMinusEmpiricalRar.unit: mean per-galaxy squared log10 residual difference (modelA - modelB)

method.likelihood: Gaussian residuals in log10 acceleration with the predeclared 0.05 dex systematic floor
method.massToLightPriors: lognormal: disk 0.5 and bulge 0.7, both sigma=0.1 dex
method.transformations: R′=R D′/D; Vk′=Vk sqrt(D′/D); Vobs′=Vobs sin(i)/sin(i′)
method.split: The galaxy holdout remains untouched by the global a0 fit; nuisance priors are external measurements.
method.fairness: The identical nuisance likelihood and priors are applied to every compared gravity law.

interpretation.scope: External galaxy-rotation holdout with a symmetric hierarchical nuisance profile
caveats: The reported nuisance calculation is a maximum-posterior profile, not a full posterior integral.
The SPARC sample is not independent of the discovery of the radial-acceleration relation.
Lensing, Solar-System, binary-pulsar, gravitational-wave and cosmological tests remain outstanding.
